question: If the self is not truly an agent, who could bear agency even figuratively?
premises: Prakṛti is not declared to be the seer of the seeing self.
No other candidate exists to take over agency from the self.
Figurative agency still requires some locus to which it can be attributed.
inference: Therefore, there is no suitable bearer for even a figurative attribution of agency.
plain_english: Prakṛti is not called the seer of the self, and there is no other candidate left; so there is no one to whom agency could even be figuratively assigned.
